newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday February 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday February 12.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime Minister Romano Prodi said he does not rule out pensions' reform but added that this should not be carried out in a hurry, and should involve all social and political counterparts. Prodi also forecast a speculative "assault on the lira" if Italy fails to join EMU from the beginning (all).
* The managing director of state railway, Giancarlo Cimoli, was put under investigation following a high-speed train derailment in which eight people were killed (all).

* In his first speech as a chairman of the bicameral commission aimed at carrying out constitutional reforms, PDS party leader Massimo D'Alema said it would be hypocrite if the commission did not also deal with the electoral reform (all).
* At Tuesday's auction the gross yields of three, six and twelve month Treasury bills fell below six percent, the lowest level in 30 years.

* The chairman of investment bank Mediobanca Francesco Cingano said the government should transfer to the Treasury, as it did with telecom holding Stet, Italy's five main banks, namely Cariplo, Banca di Roma, BNL, Montepashi and San Paolo and then start a privatisation process (all).
* Stet confirmed there have been contacts with U.S. telecoms group GTE. Stet is said to be in formal negotiations for an alliance with GTE and Canadian operator Teleglobe (all).
* Six bids have been admitted for consideration in the final phase of the process to privatise yellow pages' publisher Seat (all).

* Shares in broadcasting group Mediaset fell 3.37 percent on the Milan stock exchange after France's Canal Plus announced a 2.0 billion francs issue expiring in 2002 and exchangeable into shares of Mediaset. The move was seen as a sign that Canal Plus, once the planned merger with Nethold is completed, wants to step out of Mediaset by selling its 6.5 percent stake in television holding Fininvest (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
